name: Sticky CPT
author: Kantari Samy

sections.description:
The plugin allows to highlight the CPT in the same way as would the WordPress core functionality for posts.
You can highlight new content created for your CPT.
It is also possible to highlight the content quickly thanks to quick edit and bulk actions.

The sticky checkbox is available in the block editor, in the classic editor, in quick edit and in bulk edit, for every public custom post type.
Sticky items are stored in the core sticky_posts option, exactly like sticky posts: is_sticky() works out of the box.

Start example

$args = array(
    'post_type'      => ['project'],
    'post_status'    => 'publish',
    'posts_per_page' => -1,
    'post__in'       => get_option( 'sticky_posts' )
);
$stickyProject = new WP_Query( $args );

Hook available

add_filter( 'sticky_cpt_add_cpt' , 'add_cpt' );

function add_cpt( $post_types ) {
    $post_types['newcpt'] = 'newcpt';
    return $post_types;
}
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/sticky-cpt directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
sections.faq:
Does my custom post type need the `custom-fields` support?

No. Since 3.0.0 the block editor uses the native sticky field of the REST API. Your custom post type only needs show_in_rest to use the block editor.

Who can stick a content?

Users who can both publish and edit others’ contents of the custom post type, the same rule WordPress applies to posts.

I was reading the `sticky_value_cpt` post meta, what should I do?

This meta was removed in 3.0.0. Use is_sticky( $post_id ) or get_option( 'sticky_posts' ) instead.

How are sticky contents synchronized between Polylang translations?

Enable “Sticky posts” in the Polylang synchronization settings. Until 2.0.0 the sticky state was carried by a custom field, so it followed the “Custom fields” synchronization. Since 3.0.0 it only follows the “Sticky posts” synchronization.

Known issue with Polylang: a bulk edit unsticks translated contents

When the Polylang “Sticky posts” synchronization is enabled, a bulk edit that leaves the “Sticky” field on “No Change” unsticks the edited contents and their translations. This comes from Polylang (observed with Polylang 3.8.10) and also affects regular posts, with or without this plugin. Until it is fixed in Polylang, select “Sticky” explicitly in the bulk edit form when all the selected contents are sticky, or stick them again afterwards.
sections.changelog:
3.0.0

  • Rewrite: the sticky state now relies on the native sticky REST field, the custom-fields support is no longer required for the block editor.
  • Breaking: the sticky_value_cpt post meta is removed and deleted on update. Use is_sticky() or the sticky_posts option.
  • Breaking: with Polylang, the sticky state no longer follows the “Custom fields” synchronization. Enable the “Sticky posts” synchronization instead.
  • Security: only users allowed to publish and edit others’ contents of the post type can stick or unstick a content.
  • Fix: a sticky content is no longer unstuck when it is saved from the block editor with meta boxes, or from quick edit on hierarchical post types.
  • Fix: duplicated IDs in the sticky_posts option and wrong sticky counter.
  • Fix: stray text printed in the classic editor footer.
  • Performance: the sticky counter of the list screen no longer loads every ID of the post type.
  • Block editor script migrated to wp.editor.PluginPostStatusInfo.
  • Requires WordPress 6.6 and PHP 8.2. Tested with WordPress 7.1.

2.0.0

  • 19 march 2020
  • Gutenberg compatibility

1.0.1

  • 04 july 2017
  • Add contributor Whodunit and Check compatibility WordPress 4.8

1.0.0

  • 22 oct 2016
  • Initial release \o/
